headline: City staff outline options to replace construction-cost landscaping budgets for commercial and infill projects.
summary: Staff said current rules, at least 20 years old, base the landscaping budget on building construction costs. A BETA Technologies speaker said its buildings would push that cost to about a million dollars. There was agreement to move away from building costs, and staff expects to bring something back. The vote on LDR 2611 was held until the next meeting.
decisions: Voted 5-0 in favor of LDR 2611, the Act 250 Tier 1A review amendment, with final action held until the next meeting.
discussion: Landscaping budget formula: Staff and members discussed replacing construction-cost percentages with land area, footprint, or employee counts, and allowing more items to count toward the budget. A BETA Technologies speaker said its buildings would push landscaping costs to about a million dollars.

Civic space rules: Staff asked whether the civic space requirement for commercial and industrial areas should drop from 10% to 5% when no homes are included. Members raised when such space must be built, and whether it should be central or linear.

Long-term care in MSN district: Staff drafted rules to allow long-term care facilities in the MSN district, with housing mix standards for subdivisions. Members raised concerns about building form, streets, and whether a site would connect to surrounding neighborhoods.

Commercial size limits: Staff proposed lowering the medium scale limit from 20,000 to 15 and measuring some uses by footprint instead of floor area. Members asked whether mixed uses could stack within height limits.

decision_evidence.quote: Okay, uh this is a vote in the affirmative. Yep. Aye. Aye. Okay, that's all five unanimous... Okay, so we will hold hold over this vote results to our next meeting.

decision_titles: Amendment LDR 2611: Act 250 condition review in City Center
